To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) unsupervised pre-training is not just learning artifacts in data annotation; (ii) external knowledge from human resources is not always helpful; (iii) unsupervised external knowledge is more useful for NLI than human created external knowledge

1) pretraining is helpful on NLI, but it does not learn true inference knowledge; 2) external knowledge from human created resources is not useful for NLI; 3) external knowledge from unsupervised pretrainign is helpful for NLI, and it is more useful for NLI than for other downstream tasks.
(1) unsupervised pre-training helps NLI in the way that it helps many other tasks; i.e. by learning language modeling and sentence representation, and not by learning artifacts of NLI annotation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1) How does unsupervised pre-training help NLI models? 2) How does knowledge enhanced help NLI models, and how does it help compared to unsupervised pre-train?
three questions: (i) how does unsupervised pretrain help NLI, (ii) how does external knowledge from human resources help NLI, and (iii) how does external unsupervised knowledge help NLI.
three main questions: 1) How do unsupervised pretrainings help NLI? 2) How do knowledge enhanced models help NLI? and 3) How can we combine them to further boost performance?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two ways of adding external knowledge to NLI models do not help in the same way. In particular
the pretraining and the knowledge enhanced model have different strengths.
the pretraining and external knowledge help NLI in different ways, and that they should be combined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two types of external knowledge are not the same and they help NLI differently.
pretraining and knowledge enhanced models have a lot of similarities, and both of them can help to some extent, but they are not the same, and they are complementary to each other.

1) Pretraining helps NLI in a more general way than the artifact of data annotation; 2) Knowledge enhanced model is more effective in learning from external knowledge than pretraining, and the knowledge enhanced model can learn more from external knowledge than the pretraining one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two types of external knowledge are not interchangeable.
the two paradigms are complementary, and they both help to some extent.
the pretraining and the external knowledge are both important for NLI.
